observed: 22/33 drivable L48 pads: one af.exe build per pad with a DESIGN_ASF `set_config -loc <x> <y> <z> CFG_PULL_UP 1'b1` differs from a 4-build no-asf reference ensemble at exactly one single-set-bit position each, all inside the regenerated [0:164] preamble region; PIN_26's independently measured CFG_OPEN_DRAIN bit sits at its pull-up anchor +2 bits (chain base +3), exactly matching the decoded SINGLE-chain field order (INPUT_EN,PULL_UP,SLR,OPEN_DRAIN,PDRCTRL[4],KEEP[2]) and PIN_16's byte default 0x20 = PDRCTRL 0010 in bits 4-7.
scope: Config-encoding location only for the 22 rows of io_pad_electrical_L48.csv (sha256 d5e0c7bdd1b4229179d7aeb35b2bdb91fe8f4a077b641c8da305680fdea219f8): per-pad CFG_PULL_UP raw-image bit positions, plus PIN_26 CFG_OPEN_DRAIN. af.exe route nondeterminism (~22-33 bytes per rebuild, confined to the design routing band) was excluded by the reference-ensemble intersection. Establishes no electrical behavior by itself.

observed: Both images FCB-configured (FCB_STAT 0x000f0002). Pico GP6 on PIN_16, drive-low-then-release x3 per side: A (CFG_PULL_UP clear) read 0,0,0; B (bit set, raw offset 90 bit 1) read 1,1,1, and B read 1 even against the Pico's active pull-down.
scope: Weak pull-up behavior of CFG_PULL_UP on PIN_16 (L48, SRAM-only): the single measured bit flips the released-line level from holding low to restoring high. Anomaly recorded: with A loaded and the node pre-charged high, one pull-down read returned 1 (keeper-like hold-up on an undriven pad); the drive-low-release discriminator was 3/3 clean on both sides. No pull-up strength value and no other-pad claim.

observed: Firmware toggles GPIO2.0 (fabric-routed to PIN_26) at ~500 Hz after FCB config. Pico GP13 SCAN: A (open-drain clear) TOGGLE under pull-up AND pull-down (100/100 each); C (CFG_OPEN_DRAIN set, raw offset 10 bit 7) TOGGLE under pull-up (100/100; 103/97) but LOW 0/200 under pull-down, reproduced x3.
scope: Open-drain behavior of CFG_OPEN_DRAIN on PIN_26 (L48, SRAM-only): with the bit set the driven-high phase floats and only an external pull-up restores the high level; the low phase is driven. Push-pull control image differs only in the one measured bit plus benign route-band wobble. No electrical parameter values and no other-pad claim.

observed: For 11 pad sites (PIN_2, PIN_10, PIN_11, PIN_12, PIN_21, PIN_32, PIN_33, PIN_34, PIN_35, PIN_45, PIN_46) the identical set_config CFG_PULL_UP mechanism executed without error yet produced NO reproducible image change: double builds per pad intersected against a no-op-asf control left no stable single-bit candidate (recurring in-band candidates appeared across DIFFERENT pads, identifying them as route wobble, not per-pad config).
scope: Recorded boundary, not a defect: the special-function pad sites (flash SPI, JTAG-suspect cluster (0,1,2..5), (20,13,1..3), (14,13,2), (19,0,1/3)) do not take CFG_PULL_UP through the vendor set_config path, so io_pad_electrical_L48.csv deliberately omits them and AGaMEMnon emission fails closed for them. Their electrical-config mechanism (different chain type or protected fields) is an open question.

observed: Falsifiable test of the pad-chain model derived from the two silicon anchors (per-pad slice with PULL_UP at offset 0 and OPEN_DRAIN at offset +2, LSB-first, 6-bit stride between adjacent pads: PIN_13/14/15/16 anchors at absolute bits 703/709/715/721). PREDICTION: PIN_16's CFG_OPEN_DRAIN must land at byte 90 bit 3. A vendor set_config build of CFG_OPEN_DRAIN on PIN_16 changed exactly byte 90 bit 3 -- prediction CONFIRMED on a second pad and a second field. PREDICTION FAILED for CFG_KEEP: 2'b01 on PIN_16 was predicted at byte 91 bits 0-1 but landed at byte 89 bit 1 (absolute bit 713), eight bits BELOW the pad's own PULL_UP anchor.
scope: Encoding only. The PULL_UP/OPEN_DRAIN intra-pad spacing and the 6-bit inter-pad stride are model-confirmed; CFG_KEEP's placement is measured but UNEXPLAINED by that model and is recorded as an open question rather than modelled. A 6-bit per-pad stride cannot hold all decoded SINGLE-chain fields (INPUT_EN, PULL_UP, SLR, OPEN_DRAIN, PDRCTRL[4], KEEP[2] = 10 bits), so fields are evidently not all contiguous per pad -- do not extrapolate positions for unmeasured fields.

observed: CFG_KEEP 2'b01 on PIN_16 (byte 89 bit 1): the probe drove the pad high, released, and read 1 three times, then drove low, released, and read 0 three times. The BASELINE image with CFG_KEEP clear behaved IDENTICALLY -- 1/1/1 after driving high and 0/0/0 after driving low.
scope: NEGATIVE / NULL RESULT, recorded to prevent a false positive: an undriven AG32 pad already retains its last driven level (charge retention with very low leakage, or an always-on hold), so a drive-and-release protocol CANNOT discriminate CFG_KEEP. Bus-keeper behavior is therefore NOT qualified and no keeper claim is made. Two consequences worth keeping: (1) this explains the hold-up anomaly recorded in the PIN_16 pull-up trial, and (2) it confirms the pull-up qualification used the correct discriminator -- drive LOW then release, where the baseline holds 0 and only the pull-up forces 1, i.e. the pull-up actively overcomes the retained charge. Distinguishing CFG_KEEP would need a load that decays the node (an external resistor to the opposite rail sized above the keeper's drive but below the pull-up's), which this harness does not have.

observed: Explicit correction to an earlier record in this ledger. Trial io-electrical-pullup-anchors-22pads-20260814 described PIN_26's open-drain offset as 'exactly matching the decoded SINGLE-chain field order (INPUT_EN,PULL_UP,SLR,OPEN_DRAIN,PDRCTRL[4],KEEP[2])'. That inference is only partly supported: the PULL_UP -> OPEN_DRAIN spacing of +2 is confirmed on two pads, but the measured inter-pad stride is 6 bits, which cannot contain the 10 bits that field list implies, and CFG_KEEP does not sit where the list predicts (see io-electrical-chain-model-prediction-test-20260814).
scope: The surviving, evidence-backed claims are exactly: the 22 measured CFG_PULL_UP bit positions, the PIN_26 and PIN_16 CFG_OPEN_DRAIN positions, the +2 PULL_UP-to-OPEN_DRAIN spacing, and the 6-bit inter-pad stride. The full per-pad field layout is NOT established and positions for unmeasured fields must be measured, not derived.
